subject.title: Telegram should not create user-visible threads for internal sub-agent runs

question: Should Telegram permit child forum-topic creation only for an explicit `sessions_spawn(thread:true)` request while ordinary subagent runs remain on the parent/current conversation by default?
rationale: Current source establishes a quiet normal placement, while the related open feature and PR pursue an explicit child-topic capability; choosing the permanent user-visible contract cannot be inferred from this report alone.

options.title: Keep child topics explicit
options.body: Preserve `current` as the ordinary Telegram placement and allow child-topic binding only after an explicit thread request, with regression coverage for both paths.

options.title: Disallow Telegram child-topic spawns
options.body: Reject or remove the explicit child-topic capability so all Telegram subagent activity stays parent-routed, trading persistent child conversations for a simpler UX.

options.title: Add a user preference
options.body: Offer a documented opt-in policy only if the existing explicit tool contract cannot adequately express the desired user choice.

recommendation.title: Keep child topics explicit
recommendation.body: Preserve `current` as the ordinary Telegram placement and allow child-topic binding only after an explicit thread request, with regression coverage for both paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The active related implementation proposal already defines the explicit-thread boundary that needs an owner decision.
